lead_with.title: Not a partnership, a location option
lead_with.text: Reframe: Finance Montréal is not asking Citi to partner. It helps banks **place teams** in Montreal. The question for Kanika is whether any **FX structuring, pricing, quant, risk or middle-office** work supporting her book could sit in Montreal.

lead_with.title: New York hours at about half the cost
lead_with.text: Montreal is in the **same time zone as New York**. A Finance Montréal-commissioned Boyd Company 2026 study puts a 150-FTE financial support operation at about **US$18.9M/yr in Montreal vs US$35.3M in New York**. Useful for an Americas-hours FX coverage or follow-the-sun model with Singapore and London.

lead_with.title: Citi is already growing in Canada
lead_with.text: Citi Canada's CEO said in July 2026 the bank plans about **1,000 more hires** in Canada and that its Mississauga hub **competes with about 20 other Citi hubs for global mandates**. Montreal (with the IFC tax credit) is a way to win some of those mandates in Canada.

company.text: Citigroup is a US global bank organised around Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth and US Personal Banking. **Markets** (which includes FX) earned **$22.0B in 2025**, with **Rates and Currencies at $11.4B (+12%)**. In Asia, Citi has been **hiring FX specialists**: seven senior FX hires across Japan, Asia North, Australia and Asia South (incl. Singapore) between Sep and Nov 2025. In Canada, Citi has offices in **Toronto (HQ), Montreal, Calgary, Vancouver and Mississauga** (about 3,500 staff at the Mississauga tech hub) and is investing in its sites, **including Montreal**.

financials.text: **FY2025:** revenue **$85.2B** (+6%), net income **$14.3B** (+13%), diluted EPS **$6.99** (+18%), RoTCE **7.7%**. **Markets $22.0B** (+11%); Fixed Income Markets **$16.2B** (+10%); **Rates and Currencies $11.4B** (+12%; FX is not reported separately). Services $21.3B (+8%). About **226,000 staff** at Dec 31, 2025 (-1%). Source: Citi 4Q25 earnings release, Jan 14, 2026. 2026 quarterly figures not included here.

industry.title: Banks are re-cutting their location maps
industry.text: Global banks run networks of hubs that compete for mandates on cost and talent. Citi Canada describes exactly this competition for its Mississauga hub.

industry.title: Montreal's financial depth
industry.text: Finance Montréal cites **120,000+ finance and insurance professionals** and **150,000+ tech specialists**, and lists **Morgan Stanley, State Street, BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole and Squarepoint** among institutions that chose Montreal.

industry.title: IFC tax credit
industry.text: Quebec's International Financial Centre measure gives up to **C$18,000 per eligible employee per year** for international financial transactions (e.g. securities trading, portfolio management), third-party admin support (settlement, clearing) and some outsourced services (compliance, data, IT). Whether **FX structuring** roles qualify is **to be confirmed** case by case.

industry.title: AI and quant talent
industry.text: Montreal is known for AI research and quantitative finance talent (risk, trading, IT), plus Station Fintech, Canada's largest fintech hub per Finance Montréal. Relevant for FX pricing, analytics and automation.

talking_points: Where does her team's **pricing, risk, quant and middle-office support** sit today (Singapore, London, New York, Mumbai, other Citi hubs)?
Does Citi need **Americas-hours coverage** for FX structuring, and is New York cost a constraint?
Is she aware Citi has had a **Montreal office since 1919** and is expanding in Canada? Who at Citi decides on new hub locations?
Would a short **cost and IFC-credit comparison** (Montreal vs New York/London) for a small FX support team be useful to share internally?
Could she **introduce Noza** to the Citi Canada or Markets operations person who owns location decisions?
